about: /riven shaderprops adapts the client's active shader pack to a Riven world in a copy named <pack>-riven. A modded block joins the block.properties entry of the vanilla anchor it behaves like: the first matching rule wins, except that property rules add one entry per matching value. A riven: biome joins every numeric in(biome, ...) list in shaders.properties that holds its vanilla twin, looked up by parent/precipitation, then parent; a listed ID that is a riven: biome in this world stays only where its twin is listed. Rain hills, taiga and stone beaches have no twin: packs list their vanilla IDs as cold above vanilla snow lines (BSL: Y93 and Y123), which Riven terrain passes almost everywhere, so their own temperatures decide snow. lightAtLeast holds for a block whose default state gives at least that light: a full cube that gives light (the deep realms' moonstone, molten seams, soul ash and boundary rock) joins glowstone, which packs make emissive; BSL 10.1.8 lights a pixel by its brightness and saturation, so the glowing streaks of those textures shine and the rock around them does not. Shader IDs always come from the pack; an anchor the pack lacks is reported, not invented.
